symptom_text: A rugby player says he feels dizzy and lightheaded after a long sprint drill. He sits down, answers all questions correctly, and can walk steadily to the water cooler.
notes: Practice case: dizziness alone is a heat symptom, not a CNS sign.

symptom_text: A gardener working in full sun keeps veering off the path while carrying a hose and cannot seem to walk in a straight line. He says he is fine and knows his own name.
notes: Practice case: loss of balance / unable to walk straight is a CNS sign.

symptom_text: A field hockey player snaps at her coach for no clear reason, throws her stick, and shouts that everyone is against her. Her teammates say this is completely unlike her.
notes: Practice case: sudden irritable, combative, out-of-character behavior.

symptom_text: A student helper at a track meet feels hot and a bit annoyed that the heat is making her sweat so much, but she is chatting normally and only wants more water.
notes: Practice case: mild annoyance with sweating is not irritability as a CNS sign; heat symptom (sweating) present.

symptom_text: A hiker sits down on the trail and says his legs are cramping badly. He is sweating, alert, and tells his friends exactly how far they have walked.
notes: Practice case: cramping with normal orientation.

symptom_text: A player collapses on the field during a hot afternoon game, lies still for several seconds, then does not respond to the coach's questions and stares past him.
notes: Practice case: collapse with altered responsiveness.

symptom_text: A cyclist feels very tired after a ride, with no sweating issues, dizziness, nausea, or cramps. He is alert, drinking water, and says he just needs a nap.
notes: Practice case: fatigue is a listed heat symptom under this rule; deliberately simple.

symptom_text: A coach reports an athlete stood up too fast after stretching, felt a head rush for a few seconds, and then felt completely normal. No sweating, nausea, or cramps.
true_label: Not Heat Illness — no thermal stress indicated
notes: Practice case: brief head rush that resolved, no heat-related symptoms.

symptom_text: A lifeguard on a hot beach looks flushed and says she is very weak. She speaks clearly, knows where she is and who is on duty, and is sipping water.
notes: Practice case: forehead reading above 40.5 C with no CNS signs.

symptom_text: A runner finishing a race seems to be having a seizure and is unresponsive afterward; bystanders say he had been running in the afternoon heat.
